channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Campanha de Lula sobre força da direita no mundo: O vento sopra contra nós
item.description: Lula's campaign analyzes the first round of elections in light of a global trend toward strengthening the right. Flávio Bolsonaro is viewed as part of an international scenario where conservative parties achieve good electoral results.

item.title: Por que PSOL deixou de fazer 6 deputados apesar de recorde de Erika Hilton
item.description: Despite Erika Hilton's record 1.58 million votes, PSOL lost six seats in the Chamber of Deputies. The gap between her individual success and the party's overall weak performance, combined with strategic errors and over-reliance on a single candidate, explains the reduced representation. Political polarization and economic concerns also drove voter fragmentation.

item.title: Lula recebe governadores do PI, da BA e do CE no Alvorada
item.description: President Lula met with re-elected governors at Palácio da Alvorada: Rafael Fonteles (Piauí), Elmano de Freitas (Ceará), and Jerônimo Rodrigues (Bahia), all from the PT party. Their re-election in the first round strengthens the petivist base supporting Lula's re-election campaign heading toward the 2026 elections.

item.title: Deltan diz que pauta mais urgente é tirar Lula do poder
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol expressed support for Flávio Bolsonaro and stated that the main opposition priority is preventing Lula's reelection. He viewed the first-round results as a positive signal for the anti-PT campaign.

item.title: Flávio diz que negocia com Republicanos e Tarcísio articula apoio
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) began negotiations with the Republicanos to broaden support in the second round, with São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas leading the alliance. He thanked Romeu Zema (Novo) for support and announced a stop in Goiânia to receive Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), with convergence on security, health, AI, and mining.

item.title: Cartilha orienta apoiadores de Paes a descolar de Lula no segundo turno
item.description: Eduardo Paes' (PSD) campaign distributes a pamphlet advising supporters to avoid national polarization between Lula and Bolsonaro, suggesting that votes for governor and president can differ. The strategy aims to attract undecided voters and broaden support in the second round, especially given the strong Bolsonarist presence in the state.

item.title: “O Supremo precisa deixar de ser uma delegacia de polícia”
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho, campaign coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro, criticized the STF for viewing judicial actions and public threats from ministers as a 'police delegation,' referencing a Globo report. He argued for the judiciary's independence without interfering in the electoral process.

item.title: Flávio mira 33 milhões de abstencionistas no 2º turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, presidential candidate from PL, stated he aims to reach the 33 million voters who abstained in the first round. He emphasized that many voters stayed away due to disappointment with politics and sees these non-voters as a base to expand his electoral support in the second round. His strategy focuses on engaging new voters dissatisfied with the current political system.

item.title: Lula almoça com petistas do Nordeste e se prepara para sabatina do JN
item.description: Lula meets with Northeast PT leaders and prepares for a Jornal Nacional interview, defining strategies for the runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro. Meetings at Alvorada Palace include governors and senators, focusing on debates and a regionally targeted schedule.

item.title: Após eleição, Augusto Cury tenta transformar seu plano de governo em novo best-seller
item.description: After securing third place in the presidential race, Augusto Cury launches the book 'O Brasil dos Nossos Sonhos', compiling his government plan submitted by Avante. The work includes proposals such as ending presidential re-election, eight-year terms for Supreme Court justices, and converting high school into technical education, though its campaign connection sparked internal criticism within the party.

item.title: Flávio critica PEC da 6x1 e volta a defender regime por hora: "Liberdade"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) criticized the government's PEC to reduce the workday and advocated an alternative proposal allowing workers to negotiate their own hours, prioritizing freedom and flexibility. He also proposed private nursery vouchers for mothers needing to balance work and childcare.

item.title: Rogério Marinho diz que ‘Supremo precisa deixar de ser uma delegacia de polícia’
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho criticized the STF's performance, calling it a 'police station' and advocating for a Judiciary reform so the court focuses solely on constitutional jurisdiction. He accuses justices of using the press and investigations to oversee Congress, hindering parliamentary activity.

item.title: ‘Império em Transe’ recebe Vera Chaia e Cláudio Couto para debater a interferência dos EUA no Brasil
item.description: The 'Império em Transe' cycle examines U.S. interference in the Brazilian election, analyzing tariffs and sovereignty pressures. Vera Chaia and Cláudio Couto discuss the geopolitical implications for the vote.

item.title: Os eleitos/Filipe Barros: ‘Precisamos rediscutir qual Supremo Tribunal Federal nós queremos'
item.description: Filipe Barros, elected senator from Paraná, advocates for a broad reform of the STF, including term limits for justices and impeachment of those accused of abuses. He highlights the judiciary's credibility crisis as an electoral factor and supports measures such as banning betting markets and ending the 6x1 scale.

item.title: Candidata do PL tem mais votos que 2 eleitos da esquerda, mas fica de fora
item.description: Mariana Naime (PL) missed out on a seat in the Chamber of Deputies despite receiving 67,218 votes, more than the elected Agnelo Queiroz (PT) and Professor Reginaldo Veras (PV). The proportional system distributes seats based on the party's overall performance.

item.title: Segurança pública une Flávio Bolsonaro e Ronaldo Caiado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado met in Goiânia to seal support for the second round, with Caiado possibly joining as Public Security minister. The 'AI Against Crime' program in Goiás stands out for high arrest rates and reduced violence.

item.title: Moraes pede parecer da PGR sobre visita de Flávio ao pai
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered the Attorney General's Office to issue an opinion on Flávio Bolsonaro's request to visit his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest. The defense requested the end of restrictions imposed in July 2026, arguing no new facts justify maintaining the ban. The restriction period ends on October 11, two weeks before the election runoff.

item.title: O estado onde o eleitor está mais dividido entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: In Amapá, the presidential race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro was extremely tight, with Lula winning by just 225 votes, a mere 0.04% advantage. Despite the close presidential contest, centrist candidates performed well in state elections, defeating allies of Lula.

item.title: Brasileiro preso por usar fantasia do ICE teve de pagar fiança de R$ 29,5 mil
item.description: Brazilian Danilo Silva was arrested in the U.S. for dressing as an ICE agent to intimidate voters, posting $5,650 bail. A judge scolded him, citing election intimidation and illegal use of police insignia.

item.title: Mais de 9 mil votaram em candidato a deputado de SP preso por elo com PCC
item.description: Danilo Morgado, a candidate for state deputy in São Paulo and arrested for alleged ties to the PCC, received over 9,000 votes in the 2026 elections, becoming a substitute for the PL at the Alesp. Despite being in custody, his campaign remained active on social media, sharing a video of his mother voting. The Supreme Federal Court denied his habeas corpus on the eve of the election.

item.title: TSE diz que problema no 'processamento de dados' interrompeu divulgação de votos por quase uma hora e prepara mudança para 2º turno
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) stated that a data processing bottleneck interrupted the national broadcast of presidential election results for approximately 50 minutes, resolved by 8:04 PM. The issue only affected the 'Brazil' view of the presidential race, without impacting vote counting or state-level results. TSE is developing a technical routine for the second round and confirms that ballot data remained intact.

item.title: Flávio x Lula: a disputa dos presidenciáveis pelo apoio dos partidos do Centrão
item.description: Following the first round, Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula compete for centrist backing, with internal divisions in parties. Tarcísio de Freitas and Ronaldo Caiado support Flávio, while Hugo Motta maintains a civil stance. Parties like PSD, União Brasil, and MDB allow members freedom to choose.

item.title: Mineira Ana Elisa e outros jovens eleitos falarão com Lula sobre estratégia
item.description: President Lula scheduled meetings in Brasília to discuss strategies for the second round of elections, including gatherings with young elected officials and digital influencers. Ana Elisa and other Minas Gerais parliamentarians will join a discussion focused on social media mobilization.

item.title: Janja diz que Flávio Bolsonaro pode “silenciar” mulheres se eleito
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming his election could silence women and encourage children to have weapons. She questioned the senator's behavior toward his wife and warned of risks under a potential presidential term. Her statement is part of criticism during the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: Caiado declara apoio a Flávio três semanas após chamá-lo de um dos 'maiores assaltantes do Brasil'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, fifth-place finisher in the first round with 2.18% of valid votes, will receive Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia to endorse the PL candidate for the Presidency, three weeks after calling him one of the 'biggest looters in Brazil'. The meeting marks a shift in Caiado's stance, who initially criticized Flávio.

item.title: O caminho de Lula para turbinar a comunicação da campanha no segundo turno
item.description: Lula plans to strengthen campaign communication in the second round by bringing in professionals from winning teams in Bahia, Ceará and Piauí, while intensifying the role of reelected northeastern governors and senators. The strategy aims to offset a reduced presidential presence in the Southeast and expand his vote in the Northeast, following digital communication models of progressive lawmakers.

item.title: Moraes manda PGR se manifestar sobre pedido de Bolsonaro para liberar visitas de Flávio
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF ordered the PGR to issue an opinion on former President Jair Bolsonaro's request to resume visits from his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The decision was made following the case's progress in the Supreme Court.

item.title: Uma vez mais
item.description: The article warns about the risks of a potential second Bolsonaro government, comparing it to an authoritarian regression similar to 1964, with increased violence, social persecution, and threats to democratic freedoms. The author advocates raising political ambitions to inspire society and prevent tragic repetitions of Brazilian history.

item.title: Pesquisas do 2º turno: quando é a 1ª rodada e outras datas importantes da reta final da eleição 2026
item.description: The first round of electoral polls for the 2026 runoff election will be released this week, with institutes such as Datafolha, PoderData, and Ipespe already registered. The runoff will take place on October 25, featuring Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula as the main candidates. A second round is expected in at least five states, plus the Federal District, depending on the annulment of votes for Anthony Garotinho in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que Alcolumbre quer votar fim da 6 X 1 antes do 2º turno
item.description: The Lula administration moves forward in attempting to approve the PEC that ends the 6X1 schedule in the Senate, supported by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The vote is expected before the second round of elections on October 25th. The measure is one of Lula's main campaign flags for the second round.

item.title: Fachin se reúne com líder de Lula e coordenador de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The president of the Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, held a series of meetings with party leaders following the first round of the 2026 elections, including discussions with the campaign coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro and the leader of Lula's government in the Senate. The talks focused on institutional stability and the judiciary's stance amid the growth of the PL in Congress.

item.title: As atenções agora se voltam para 2028
item.description: Following the 2026 elections, which determined governors, senators, and federal and state representatives, attention in the Brazilian political landscape now turns to the 2028 municipal elections, where mayors and city councilors will be elected. This new electoral cycle promises to bring debates on local governance, security, health, education, and infrastructure in Brazilian cities.

item.title: Flávio espera receber apoio de presidente do União e de deputado estadual mais votado do Rio
item.description: The national president of União Brasil, Antônio de Rueda, is expected to support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the presidential race and Douglas Ruas in the Rio gubernatorial race. The inclusion of Rueda and Márcio Canella on the presidential slate strengthens PL's political network in the Baixada Fluminense, a strategic region for both campaigns.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva claims to be the only anti-system candidate, criticizing the Brazilian Supreme Court for 'promiscuity' in politics. The post includes a poll comparing Lula and Flávio Dino, highlighting debates on corruption and the judiciary.

item.title: “Algumas perdas não têm volta”, diz campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula's campaign released a video highlighting achievements such as the 6X1 work schedule, Popular Pharmacy, minimum wage increases, and pension adjustments while warning about irreversible losses in the 2026 elections. The content targets the runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, who led in the first round.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula: as propostas dos candidatos à Presidência que disputam o 2º turno
item.description: BBC News Brasil presents an interactive comparison of Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula's proposals for the 2026 presidential runoff, analyzing their stances on economy, security, health, education, environment and other key issues. The content highlights differences between the candidates across areas such as economic policy, public safety and foreign policy, providing contextualized insight for voters.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve liberar revisão criminal de Bolsonaro após 2º turno
item.description: Supreme Federal Court minister Kassio Nunes Marques is expected to review the criminal appeal filed by former president Jair Bolsonaro's defense after the October 25 runoff election. The appeal seeks to suspend Bolsonaro's 27-year sentence for attempted coup, challenging the digital evidence chain. Nunes Marques delayed the decision to avoid influencing the electoral outcome.

item.title: Nova pesquisa testa a disputa Flávio Bolsonaro x Lula no segundo turno pela primeira vez
item.description: AtlasIntel will release on Friday the 9th its first poll on the 2026 presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, measuring voting intention, voter decision-making, candidate rejection, and perceptions in areas like the economy and Supreme Court crisis. The survey maps the direct race between the two, without any other candidates, including questions on governance, political figures, and election dynamics. It will be the first snapshot of the final matchup in the 2026 election.

item.title: Saiba o que os candidatos ao Planalto farão nesta 3ª feira
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential runoff candidates, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), have separate campaign schedules on Tuesday. Lula holds coordination meetings at the Alvorada and Planalto Palaces, while Flávio travels to Goiânia for political meetings with Ronaldo Caiado and Governor Daniel Vilela.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente 3ª feira
item.description: President Lula has campaign meetings and encounters with ministers in Brasília on Tuesday, focusing on political and electoral coordination. His agenda includes events at the Alvorada Palace and the Planalto Palace, plus a campaign executive meeting in the afternoon.

item.title: 2026 repete 2022 de forma invertida e direita avança
item.description: The 2026 election mirrors 2022's outcome but with Lula trailing in the first round, reflecting rising anti-petismo and voter fatigue with statist policies. The PT repeats outdated proposals, such as formalizing app drivers with work contracts, failing to grasp the shifting political landscape in Brazil and globally.

item.title: Pesquisas mostravam avanço de Flávio antes do 1º turno
item.description: Pre-election polling data closely matched the actual results of the October 4, 2026, vote, with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) winning 47.03% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) receiving 45.16%. Most of nine surveyed firms showed Flávio gaining ground in late September and early October, while Lula held steady and second-tier candidates lost traction.

item.title: Efeito Flávio derruba juro e país economiza R$ 66 bilhões com dívida
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's victory in the first round of the 2026 elections led to a 1 percentage point drop in future interest rates, saving the government R$65.8 billion over four years. The market sees a more fiscally disciplined government under Flávio, allowing more room for interest rate cuts and economic stimulus.

item.title: Lula ou Flávio?
item.description: A poll by Arte/Metrópoles shows 64% of 6,082 readers do not believe Lula could defeat Flávio Dino in a runoff. The hypothetical matchup polarizes opinions on the feasibility of a direct electoral contest between the two leaders.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vs. Lula: o que está em disputa na política energética
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula differ in energy policy: Bolsonaro favors privatization and market logic, while Lula prioritizes sovereignty, energy supply, and transition to a low-carbon economy. The debate reflects contrasting views on the state's role in industry and technology.

item.title: Por que o palhaço Tiririca saiu de cena
item.description: Tiririca, elected in 2010 with 1.3 million votes, saw his support drop 99.6% by 2026, reflecting the decline of Brazilian electoral humor. Known for parodies and few legislative actions, he left PL and joined PSD, promising a more serious mandate. His trajectory symbolizes the wear-out of charismatic figures without legislative effectiveness.

item.title: Bancada do Rio na Câmara dos Deputados é majoritariamente masculina e de direita: dos 46 eleitos, só dez são mulheres
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro state delegation in the Chamber of Deputies remained predominantly male and right-wing, with only 10 women elected out of 46 seats. The Liberal Party (PL) led representation by securing 15 deputies, followed by center and left-wing forces. The election highlighted PL growth and losses for parties like União and Republicanos.

item.title: O anúncio que ligou o sinal de alerta na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro ainda durante a votação
item.description: The Lula government authorized a PF investigation into alleged U.S. interference in the election, following a Guardian report revealing a project allocating resources to groups critical of the STF. The measure triggered a reaction in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign during the first-round voting, with polls open. The inquiry was announced by the PF director-general, Andrei Rodrigues.

item.title: Candidatos que usaram ‘Lula’ nas urnas se saem melhor que os que adotaram ‘Bolsonaro’
item.description: Candidates who linked their campaigns to the name 'Lula' performed better electorally than those who used 'Bolsonaro', according to election data analysis. The strategy of invoking influential political figures appears to have positively impacted results.

item.title: ‘Futuro brasileiro é de hegemonia conservadora’, diz Pavanato, deputado federal mais votado em SP
item.description: Lucas Pavanato, the most voted federal deputy in São Paulo, stated that the vote reflects dissatisfaction with the STF and President Lula's government, advocating for conservative hegemony and the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes. He attributed his high vote count to resistance against the Supreme Court and criticized the Court's actions, referencing the 1932 Constitutional Revolution.
